newsitem.title: POLAND: Zloty unchanged vs basket, one-day depos inch up.
newsitem.headline: Zloty unchanged vs basket, one-day depos inch up.

text.p: The Polish zloty closed flat against the basket of currencies after a light trading session with balanced client orders and small scale speculation on dollar/mark moves on world markets, dealers said.
"We observed a lucklustre trade today with buy and sell orders balancing out and players livening up trade by small-scale speculation," said Tomasz Wolosz from BRE SA.

The zloty closed flat at 2.98/2.96 percent from the trading band centre against Wednesday's 3.03/2.95 percent. It was at 3.0762/68 to the dollar, up from 3.0820/40 on Wednesday and at 1.8155/60 to the mark, down from 1.8070/90.

Dealers said a slight rise in one-day deposit rates on Thursday was caused by fading expectations of a near term interest rate cut after Finance Minister Marek Belka said that a real rate rise was presently justified.
Belka also reinforced market expectations of flat rates by saying that the NBP would lower official interst rates no earlier than in several months or the second half of 1997.
Short-term deposit rates were quoted above 22 percent on Thursday, higher than the main central bank 14-day reverse repo rate of 21.65 percent and NBP-bill yields at 22.00 percent.
Overnight rates were at 22.5/23.0 percent against opening's 22.5/22.7 percent, and tomorrow/next rates were at 22.55/23.00 percent, up from this morning's 22.50/22.95 percent.
